title: Fractions: Halves to Eighths
seo_title: Grade 3 Fractions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Use and name fractions in familiar contexts including halves, quarters, eighths, thirds, sixths and fifths; recognise fractions in diagrammatic form; begin to recognise that two halves or three thirds make one whole; solve problems that involve equal sharing leading to solutions that include unitary and non-unitary fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 3 maths worksheets: halves, thirds, quarters, fifths, sixths and eighths of shapes and collections, and comparing fractions. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: The bottom number tells how many equal parts.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The bottom number tells how many equal parts; the top number tells how many we take.
  • More equal parts means smaller parts: 18 is smaller than 14.
  • A quarter of 20 is 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
  • Fractions sit between whole numbers on a number line.

Examples

Example

Three quarters of 12

12 ÷ 4 = 3

3 × 3

Answer: 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
All the partsCount only the shaded parts.
Bigger bottom number1/8 is smaller than 1/4.
The wrong divisionDivide by the bottom number.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the largest?
items.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top. The smallest denominator means the whole is cut into the fewest parts, so each part is biggest. 12 is the largest.

items.q: Which unit fraction is the smallest?
items.e: 10 is the biggest denominator. A whole cut into 10 equal parts has the smallest parts, so 110 is the smallest. A bigger number on the bottom does not mean a bigger fraction.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the fractions.
c: 13 < 16
13 > 16
13 = 16
items.e: Both are unit fractions. The whole is split into 3 parts or into 6 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 13 > 16.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.

18 = 14
18 < 14
items.e: Both are unit fractions. The whole is split into 8 parts or into 4 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 18 < 14.
